did_you_know.text: Did you know? After defeating Israel, the Philistines captured the Ark of God at Ebenezer and brought it to Ashdod.
Did you know? The Philistines placed the Ark of God in the temple of Dagon, beside Dagon’s statue.
Did you know? The morning after the Ark was placed there, the people of Ashdod found Dagon fallen facedown before the Ark of the Lord. But they lifted him up and put him back in his place.
Did you know? The next day, Dagon was found fallen facedown before the Ark again. This time, his head and both hands had been cut off; only his body remained.
Did you know? After Dagon fell, a custom was established in Dagon’s temple in Ashdod: to this day, the priests and all who enter the temple do not step on the threshold.
Did you know? The passage describes the plague in Ashdod and its surrounding area as the work of the Lord’s hand, and mentions afflictions called tumors, or hemorrhoids.
Did you know? When the people of Ashdod wanted to move the Ark away, they summoned the Philistine rulers and decided to transfer it to Gath.
Did you know? A great panic broke out in Gath, and everyone in the city, from the least to the greatest, was afflicted by the plague described in the chapter.
Did you know? After the Ark was moved to Ekron, the people of the city cried out, “They have brought the Ark of the God of Israel here to kill us and our people!”
Did you know? The Philistine rulers assembled at Ekron and decided to send the Ark of God back to its own place, because the plague had caused death and great panic in the city.
